account: Today I have office business at eight, a mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, and office again at sixteen thirty. The unusual addition is the builder's request to meet at the great hall entrance at 17:55 and enter at eighteen sharp. He says he wants my opinion on eight installed lanterns and the table layout. I approved it, keeping my nineteen o'clock return home unchanged. The builder was at the office unusually early and repeated the precise meeting time several times. I also noticed the innkeeper there early, though I learned no business from them. The builder is now carrying a lantern. These details suggest preparations for something in the hall, perhaps a gathering, but the stated purpose is an inspection and I have no proof of another purpose. Yesterday there was talk about a sack of bread and possible celebration or decorations; my neighbour cautioned that the bread could simply be ordinary inn supplies and reported the baker denied a celebration or decorations. The secretary's enquiries established no verified complaint or unusual quay news. I should not treat those rumours as facts. The secretary has confirmed my inspection appointment and needs one emerald for a writable book to record the addendum; I have just returned the original appointment book as requested. I intend to keep my appointments, fund the record, and learn what the hall preparations actually mean by observing and asking rather than assuming concealment.
